angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 36,819,675 km at 11955.45 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 0.0836 +/- 0.0124 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 11955.45 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 52.925 (48.563 to 58.011) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 36,819,675 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 5.207 (5.157 to 5.395) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5217 +/- 16.5 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4287715299577853696: teff_gspphot 5217.246 K (16th-84th percentiles 5201.1543-5234.086), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4287715299577853696: teff_gspphot 5217.246 K (16th-84th percentiles 5201.1543-5234.086), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gaia-dr3-4287715299577853696.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 1.707, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
